1.title: Azure Regions, Zones and Datacenters
1.text: Welcome to Module four: Azure Regions, Zones and Datacenters. It covers the exam area Describe Azure architecture and services. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Describe Azure regions, region pairs, and sovereign regions. Describe availability zones. Describe Azure datacenters. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Describe Azure architecture and services (thirty-five to forty percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A Z nine hundred study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: The physical layers of Azure
1.text: The physical layers of Azure. Azure runs on a worldwide network of datacenters. They are grouped into regions, and some regions are split into availability zones. Datacenter. A physical building with servers, power, cooling and network. Availability zone. A physically separate group of one or more datacenters inside one region, with independent power, cooling and networking. Region. A set of datacenters deployed within a latency-defined perimeter and connected by a dedicated low-latency network.

1.title: The physical layers of Azure, continued
1.text: The physical layers of Azure. Region pair. Two regions in the same geography, set up to protect each other. Geography. A market area (often a country or group of countries) that keeps data and compliance boundaries.

1.title: The physical layers of Azure, continued
1.text: The physical layers of Azure. The figure shows this: Datacenters, availability zones, regions and region pairs.

1.title: Regions
1.text: Regions. A region is where you choose to deploy a resource, for example East U S or West Europe. Most resources are tied to one region, so you pick the region when you create them. Choose a region by. Location near users (lower latency). Data residency and compliance needs (keep data in a country or area). Service availability: not every service or size is in every region. Price: the same service can cost different amounts in different regions. Exam tip: Resource location is a property of the resource. A resource group has its own location (where metadata is stored), but its resources can be in other regions.

1.title: Region pairs
1.text: Region pairs. Most regions are paired with another region in the same geography, usually hundreds of miles apart. Many newer regions have availability zones and no region pair. Benefits of a pair. Recovery priority: if there is a broad outage, one region of each pair is recovered first. Planned updates: Azure strives to stagger planned system updates across the regions of a pair, so both are not updated together. Data residency: pairs stay in the same geography (with exceptions) so data stays in the area. Some services use the pair for geo-redundant replication (for example geo-redundant storage, Module eight).

1.title: Sovereign regions
1.text: Sovereign regions. Sovereign regions are instances of Azure that are isolated from the main (public) Azure instance, to meet special legal or compliance needs. Azure Government. U S government agencies and their partners. Microsoft Azure operated by twenty-one Vianet (Azure China). Customers in China, run by a local partner. Exam tip: If a question mentions government compliance or operating in China with a local operator, think sovereign regions. They are physically and logically separate from the global Azure regions.

1.title: Availability zones
1.text: Availability zones. An availability zone (A Z) is a physically separate location inside a region. Each zone has independent power, cooling and networking. Regions that support zones have at least three of them. Use zones to protect against a failure of a single datacenter.

1.title: Availability zones, continued
1.text: Availability zones. Zonal services. Meaning: You choose the zone where the resource runs. Examples: a virtual machine placed in zone one. Zone-redundant services. Meaning: Azure replicates the resource across zones for you. Examples: zone-redundant storage, zone-redundant databases. Non-regional (always available) services. Meaning: Not tied to one region; resilient to zone and region failure. Examples: Microsoft Entra I D (Module nine). Exam tip: Zones protect inside a region (datacenter failure). Region pairs protect across regions (regional disaster). Not every region has zones. Availability sets spread V Ms across fault and update domains inside one datacenter, a weaker option than zones.

1.title: Azure datacenters
1.text: Azure datacenters. Azure datacenters are large, secured facilities with. Physical security: controlled access, monitoring. Redundant power and cooling and many network connections. A Microsoft global network that links the datacenters. Microsoft maintains the datacenters, hardware and physical network. You choose where your resources run (region and zone), not which building.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants its app to keep running if one datacenter in the region fails. Which feature should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Availability zones. Availability zones are separate locations inside a region and protect against a datacenter failure. A region pair protects against loss of a whole region.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. An agency needs a version of Azure that is isolated for U S government workloads. What is it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Azure Government (a sovereign region). Azure Government is a sovereign region built for U S government needs.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. What is true about the two regions of a region pair? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: They are in the same geography, and Azure staggers planned updates across them. Pairs sit in the same geography, usually far apart, and Azure staggers planned updates.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which is a reason to pick a particular Azure region? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Closeness to users, data residency, service availability and price. Latency, compliance, available services and price differ by region.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. What does a zone-redundant service do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Is replicated across zones automatically by Azure. Zone-redundant services spread their data or instances across zones for you. Zonal services run in one zone you choose.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. How many availability zones does a region that supports them have at least? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Three. Regions that support availability zones have at least three.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is an Azure region? Answer: A set of datacenters in a latency-defined perimeter, connected by a low-latency network. Question two. What does an availability zone have that makes it independent? Answer: Its own power, cooling and networking. Question three. Zones protect inside a region; what protects across regions? Answer: Region pairs (and geo-redundancy).

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name the two sovereign regions. Answer: Azure Government (U S) and Azure China (operated by twenty-one Vianet). Question five. What is a geography? Answer: A market area, such as a country or group of countries, that keeps data residency and compliance boundaries. Question six. Who maintains the physical datacenters? Answer: Microsoft.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Region: where you deploy; choose by latency, compliance, services, price. Region pair: same geography, usually hundreds of miles apart; staggered updates; recovery priority. Sovereign regions: Azure Government and Azure China: isolated instances for legal needs. Availability zone: separate location in a region with its own power, cooling, network; at least three. Zonal versus zone-redundant: you pick the zone versus Azure replicates across zones. Protection: zones equals datacenter failure; region pair equals regional disaster. In the next module, we continue the course.
